name: Ding Wang
title: Robotics Engineering Student

headline: Learning to build robots that understand the world.
bio: I study Robotics Engineering at Beijing Institute of Technology, in the Li Zexiang Innovation and Entrepreneurship Class. My interests span embodied AI, robot manipulation, reinforcement learning, and generative models. I work across algorithms and hardware, and share what I learn through research notes and open-source projects.
bioChinese: 我是王玎，北京理工大学特立书院机器人工程（李泽湘双创班）2024 级本科生，学业成绩优异，2026年获国家奖学金，连续三次获评校级一等奖学金。科研竞赛成果丰硕，2026年作为第一负责人主持北京市自然科学基金本科生启研计划项目，获5万元资助；累计斩获ROBOCON国一、挑战杯国二、数模国赛国二、美赛M奖等国家级以上奖项8项；主持校级大创项目2项、国创市创项目1项。学生工作履职得力，建设运营“李泽湘双创班创新实践基地”，组织深圳科创实践、杭州具身智能调研等多项班级实践活动。获评校级优秀学生、院级优秀团员、优秀朋辈导师等荣誉，综合素养全面。

en.heroImageAlt: Ding Wang at a robotics competition venue.
en.bioLong: I am Ding Wang, a Robotics Engineering undergraduate in the 2024 cohort of the Li Zexiang Innovation and Entrepreneurship Class at Teli College, Beijing Institute of Technology. My strong academic record includes a National Scholarship in 2026 and three consecutive first-class university scholarships. In 2026, I led a project under the Beijing Natural Science Foundation’s Undergraduate Research Initiation Program as its lead student investigator, with RMB 50,000 in funding. I have received eight competition awards at the national level or above, including a ROBOCON National First Prize, a Challenge Cup National Second Prize, a CUMCM National Second Prize, and an MCM/ICM Meritorious Winner award. I have also led two university-level student innovation projects and one project at the national/municipal level. My student leadership work includes developing and operating the Innovation Practice Base for the Li Zexiang Innovation and Entrepreneurship Class, and organizing class activities such as innovation and technology visits in Shenzhen and field visits to study embodied AI in Hangzhou. My honors include a university-level Outstanding Student award, a college-level Outstanding Youth League Member award, and an Outstanding Peer Mentor award, reflecting my development across academic work, research, and student leadership.
